put.description: Requires an organization administrative-context token. Creating connections and changing bindings additionally require platform administrator authority. Credentials are encrypted by the host and never included in responses. Responses use Cache-Control: private, no-store. The connection keeps its ID, library binding and in-flight acquisitions. plugin_config is merged over the saved settings: a submitted key replaces its saved value, null removes it, and an omitted key keeps it. A credential that is omitted or empty keeps its saved value only while the URL it is bound to is unchanged; a changed URL requires the credential again, and a URL cleared to an empty string or removed with null drops it. Changing qbittorrent_url or nzbget_url makes downloads already handed to the previous client fail their status checks. Silo's generic request-integration editor refuses audiobook connections. Unknown JSON fields and extra bodies are rejected.

Tokens bind actor, library, owned revision and path row identities/xmin, so a legacy path write that leaves path rows (including A-to-B-to-A) requires reload. A path set that is empty when read and empty again when saved has no row evidence; that save replaces exactly the empty set that was read. A conflict returns current_library_revision. A successful replacement that changes filesystem paths queues the ordinary library_paths_changed scan. Until native-storage library_location_mixing is true, a library keeps filesystem paths or one plugin source over its lifetime, counting retained locations; other shapes return location_mixing_unavailable. Removal retains root/location/catalog identities and disables publication memberships without deleting provider files. Provider I/O occurs before write transactions. These mutations are outside shared lifecycle idempotency: mutation_outcome_unknown requires reconciliation using the returned library_id, never automatic replay. Native audio remains unavailable until full scanner/catalog/playback composition.

post.description: Requires matching signed administrative context and current actor/library/source authority. Inspect native-storage library_location_atomic_editing first. POST reuses ordinary library validation/defaults and atomically saves paths and initial selections. Library options reject legacy storage_source. At least one filesystem path or selection is required. PUT replaces paths and selections only; both arrays must be present and nonnull, with at most 128 roots from 16 plugin sources. GET returns every retained location/root plus active selections, revision and an expiring edit_token. Disabled or unavailable roots remain visible for removal and may have no selection_ref. PUT requires expected_revision and expected_edit_token from GET. Tokens bind actor, library, owned revision and path row identities/xmin, so a legacy path write that leaves path rows (including A-to-B-to-A) requires reload. A path set that is empty when read and empty again when saved has no row evidence; that save replaces exactly the empty set that was read. A conflict returns current_library_revision. A successful replacement that changes filesystem paths queues the ordinary library_paths_changed scan. Until native-storage library_location_mixing is true, a library keeps filesystem paths or one plugin source over its lifetime, counting retained locations; other shapes return location_mixing_unavailable. Removal retains root/location/catalog identities and disables publication memberships without deleting provider files. Provider I/O occurs before write transactions. These mutations are outside shared lifecycle idempotency: mutation_outcome_unknown requires reconciliation using the returned library_id, never automatic replay. Native audio remains unavailable until full scanner/catalog/playback composition.
